description: Fix learning_interference benchmark to achieve std >= 0.10 across models
steps: Step 1: Read current task_interference.py in repo/benchmarks/learning/ and KNOWLEDGE entry on Learning Interference Scoring v2
Step 2: The v2 scoring fix was implemented but std=0.037 persists — diagnose why by running against 3 models (Opus, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B) via run_benchmark_bedrock.py
Step 3: Increase difficulty spread: add harder interference conditions (more overlapping categories, longer lists, shorter retention intervals) and easier baseline conditions
Step 4: Re-run against 3 models, verify std >= 0.10 and range >= 0.20
Step 5: Update the corresponding notebook repo/notebooks/learning_interference.ipynb to match task file changes

description: Fix exec_func_wcst benchmark to achieve std >= 0.10 (currently std=0.007)
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/executive_functions/task_wcst.py and the KNOWLEDGE entry on WCST single-trial being trivial

Step 2: Implement full 128-card Wisconsin Card Sorting Test protocol: present cards sequentially in a single prompt, require the model to sort by an unstated rule, shift rule after 10 consecutive correct without announcing the shift
Step 3: Score perseveration errors (continuing old rule after shift), categories completed, and total errors with weighted composite
Step 4: Test against Opus, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B — target std >= 0.10
Step 5: Update notebook repo/notebooks/exec_func_wcst.ipynb to match
Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/executive_functions/task_tol.py to understand current Tower of London implementation
Step 2: Diagnose floor cause: likely output parsing failures, overly hard puzzles, or unclear instructions
Step 3: Add easier 2-move and 3-move problems alongside hard ones; create 3 difficulty tiers weighted 0.20/0.30/0.50
Step 4: Fix any answer parsing issues — verify model output format matches expected extraction regex
Step 5: Test against Opus, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B — target mean >= 0.20 and std >= 0.10
Step 6: Update notebook repo/notebooks/exec_func_tol.ipynb to match

description: Fix social_cog_false_belief benchmark — ceiling effect at 0.967
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/social_cognition/task_false_belief.py
Step 2: Add 3rd-order and 4th-order nested belief scenarios (Alice thinks Bob thinks Carol believes...)
Step 3: Add false-belief scenarios with misleading surface cues that reward literal interpretation over mental state tracking
Step 4: Create 3 tiers: 1st-order (0.15 weight), 2nd-order (0.30 weight), 3rd/4th-order (0.55 weight)
Step 5: Test against Opus, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B — target mean <= 0.85 and std >= 0.10
Step 6: Update notebook repo/notebooks/social_cog_false_belief.ipynb

description: Fix social_cog_pragmatic benchmark to achieve std >= 0.10 (currently std=0.036)
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/social_cognition/task_pragmatic.py
Step 2: Add harder pragmatic inference items: indirect speech acts, conversational implicature requiring world knowledge, politeness-based indirection, Gricean maxim violations
Step 3: Add items where literal and pragmatic interpretations conflict sharply — understatement, litotes, rhetorical questions
Step 4: Create difficulty tiers: direct implicature (0.15), indirect/contextual (0.35), complex multi-layer (0.50)
Step 5: Test against Opus, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B — target std >= 0.10
Step 6: Update notebook repo/notebooks/social_cog_pragmatic.ipynb

description: Run all non-metacognition tracks against all 10 Bedrock models and compile results
steps: Step 1: Verify all benchmark fixes from prior tasks are in place (learning_interference, exec_func_wcst, exec_func_tol, social_cog_false_belief, social_cog_pragmatic)
Step 2: Run attention (4), learning (4), executive_functions (5), social_cognition (4) benchmarks against all 10 models using run_benchmark_bedrock.py with <=4 concurrent processes
Step 3: Compile results into repo/results/score_matrix_all_tracks.csv
Step 4: Generate per-track discriminatory analysis summaries in repo/results/ (mean, std, range per benchmark)

description: Draft writeups for attention, learning, executive functions, and social cognition tracks
steps: Step 1: Read repo/WRITEUP_METACOGNITION.md as the quality bar and template
Step 2: Read per-track results from repo/results/ (score matrices, discriminatory analyses)
Step 3: Draft repo/WRITEUP_ATTENTION.md — cite Posner 1980, Treisman and Gelade 1980, Wickens 2002; highlight divided/selective/sustained attention constructs
Step 4: Draft repo/WRITEUP_LEARNING.md — cite Thorndike 1932, Ausubel 1968; highlight transfer, interference, curriculum effects
Step 5: Draft repo/WRITEUP_EXECUTIVE_FUNCTIONS.md — cite Miyake 2000, Diamond 2013; highlight inhibition, shifting, updating constructs
Step 6: Draft repo/WRITEUP_SOCIAL_COGNITION.md — cite Baron-Cohen 1985, Grice 1975; highlight ToM, pragmatics, sarcasm constructs
Step 7: Each writeup must follow required template, be <= 1500 words, and include organizational affiliations section
Step 8: Generate cover images for all 4 tracks at repo/assets/{track}_cover.png — grouped bar charts similar to metacognition cover style

description: Verify all 26 benchmarks pass std >= 0.08 threshold and fix any that fail
steps: Step 1: Load repo/results/score_matrix_all_tracks.csv and compute std per benchmark across all 10 models (excluding NaN/error cells)
Step 2: List any benchmarks with std < 0.08. Likely candidates: attention_selective (was 0.054 with 3 models), learning_curves (range=0.180)
Step 3: For each failing benchmark, diagnose cause (ceiling, floor, or clustering) by examining the per-model score distribution
Step 4: For attention_selective if std < 0.08: add harder conjunction-search items with more distractors and feature-similarity confounds; retest against Opus, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B
Step 5: For learning_curves if std < 0.08: increase difficulty range by adding steeper learning curves and shorter training windows; retest against 3 models
Step 6: Update corresponding notebooks to match any task file changes
Step 7: Re-run fixed benchmarks against all 10 models and confirm std >= 0.08; update score_matrix_all_tracks.csv

description: Fix all notebook hard-rule violations listed in GOALS.md (duplicate cells, broken imports, nbconvert duplicate)
steps: Step 1: Delete repo/notebooks/exec_func_crt.nbconvert.ipynb (exact duplicate of exec_func_crt.ipynb per GOALS.md)
Step 2: Fix metacog_canary.ipynb: replace from data.canary_items import ... with inlined data; remove duplicate @kbench.task cell; remove duplicate .run() call
Step 3: Fix attention_divided.ipynb: Cell 0 and Cell 2 are 100% identical — delete Cell 2
Step 4: Fix attention_instruction_update.ipynb: same issue — delete the duplicate Cell 2
Step 5: Fix attention_vigilance.ipynb: double .run() in cell 2 + cell 3 — remove one
Step 6: Fix metacog_epistemic_revision.ipynb: double .run() in cell 1 + cell 2 — delete cell 2
Step 7: Run jupyter nbconvert --to notebook on all 6 fixed notebooks to verify syntax validity

description: Update all 5 writeups with final 10-model scores from score_matrix_all_tracks.csv
steps: Step 1: Load repo/results/score_matrix_all_tracks.csv and repo/results/per_track_analysis.md

Step 2: For each of the 5 writeups (WRITEUP_METACOGNITION.md, WRITEUP_ATTENTION.md, WRITEUP_LEARNING.md, WRITEUP_EXECUTIVE_FUNCTIONS.md, WRITEUP_SOCIAL_COGNITION.md): update results tables with final 10-model numbers
Step 3: Ensure each writeup references the correct benchmarks and scores — cross-check against score matrix
Step 4: Verify all 5 writeups remain under 1500 words after updates (use wc -w)
Step 5: Update discriminatory analysis sections with final std/range values per benchmark

description: Regenerate cover images for all 5 tracks using final 10-model scores
steps: Step 1: Load final scores from repo/results/score_matrix_all_tracks.csv

Step 2: For each track, generate a grouped bar chart at repo/assets/{track}_cover.png showing all benchmarks in that track across 5 representative models (Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Nova Pro, Llama 3.3 70B, Ministral 3B)
Step 3: Include human baseline band (0.60-0.85 green shaded region) and category shading consistent with existing metacognition cover style
Step 4: Verify all 5 images are valid PNGs at reasonable resolution (>=1000px wide, >=150 DPI)

description: Final pre-submission audit: verify all GOALS.md checklist items are met across all 5 tracks
steps: Step 1: For each of 5 tracks, verify: (a) all benchmarks have std >= 0.08 in score_matrix_all_tracks.csv, (b) all 10 models have scores, (c) writeup exists and is <= 1500 words, (d) cover image exists at repo/assets/
Step 2: Verify all notebook hard-rule fixes from GOALS.md are applied (no duplicate cells, no broken imports, no .nbconvert duplicate)
Step 3: Verify all notebooks pass jupyter nbconvert --to notebook syntax validation
Step 4: Check that all .py task files match their corresponding .ipynb notebooks (no drift since last sync audit)
Step 5: Run git status to confirm all changes are committed; if not, stage and commit with message: final pre-submission audit pass
Step 6: Output a final checklist summary with PASS/FAIL per criterion per track
Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/attention/task_selective.py and examine the current item set - likely too easy (mean=0.880, ceiling clustering)

Step 2: Add harder conjunction-search items: increase distractor count to 15-20 per trial, add feature-similarity confounds (target=red-X among red-O and blue-X distractors), add set-size scaling conditions (8/16/24 items)
Step 3: Create 3 difficulty tiers: pop-out search (0.10 weight), feature conjunction (0.40 weight), triple-conjunction with high distractor similarity (0.50 weight)
Step 4: Test against Claude Opus 4.6, Nova Pro, and Ministral 3B via run_benchmark_bedrock.py - verify std >= 0.08 and mean drops below 0.85
Step 5: Update repo/notebooks/attention_selective.ipynb to match task file changes
Step 6: Re-run against all 10 models and update repo/results/score_matrix_all_tracks.csv
Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/social_cognition/task_emotional_prosody.py - current scores cluster at 0.73-0.88 with insufficient spread
Step 2: Add harder items requiring detection of mixed/ambiguous emotions, subtle sarcasm conveyed through prosodic cues in text, and culturally-specific emotional expressions
Step 3: Add easy baseline items (clear single-emotion expressions) weighted 0.10 and hard items (conflicting verbal/prosodic signals, masked emotions) weighted 0.60, medium items weighted 0.30
Step 4: Test against Claude Opus 4.6, Nova Pro, and Ministral 3B - verify std >= 0.08
Step 5: Sync .py notebook drift flagged in KNOWLEDGE (py is ~2h newer than ipynb) - regenerate repo/notebooks/social_cog_emotional_prosody.ipynb from task file
Step 6: Re-run against all 10 models and update score_matrix_all_tracks.csv
Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/learning/task_learning_curves.py - current range is only 0.180 across models, suggesting uniform difficulty
Step 2: Add steeper learning curves requiring faster acquisition (fewer examples before test), and harder domains (abstract rule systems vs concrete pattern matching)
Step 3: Add a far-transfer condition where training and test items use different surface features but same underlying structure - weight 0.50
Step 4: Reduce training window for hard condition to 3 examples (from current) to expose learning speed differences between models
Step 5: Test against Claude Opus 4.6, Nova Pro, and Ministral 3B - verify std >= 0.08
Step 6: Update repo/notebooks/learning_curves.ipynb to match; re-run all 10 models and update score_matrix_all_tracks.csv

description: Fix metacog_error_detection benchmark discrimination (std=0.077, borderline - push above 0.08)
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_error_detection.py - current std=0.077 is borderline below 0.08 threshold

Step 2: Add 5-8 harder items with subtle errors: statistical reasoning fallacies (base rate neglect, Simpsons paradox), subtle unit conversion errors, off-by-one logical errors in multi-step arguments
Step 3: Add 3-4 easy items with obvious factual errors to anchor the low end and increase spread for weaker models
Step 4: Reweight tiers if needed to ensure hard items dominate (>=0.50 weight)
Step 5: Test against Claude Opus 4.6, Nova Pro, and Ministral 3B - verify std >= 0.08
Step 6: Update repo/notebooks/metacog_error_detection.ipynb; re-run all 10 models and update score_matrix_all_tracks.csv

description: Update all 5 writeups and cover images with post-fix benchmark scores
steps: Step 1: After attention_selective, social_cog_emotional_prosody, learning_curves, and metacog_error_detection fixes are complete and re-run against all 10 models, load updated repo/results/score_matrix_all_tracks.csv
Step 2: Update results tables in all 5 WRITEUP_*.md files with the new scores for any changed benchmarks
Step 3: Regenerate cover images at repo/assets/{track}_cover.png for any tracks with updated benchmark scores
Step 4: Verify all writeups remain under 1500 words (wc -w)
Step 5: Update discriminatory analysis sections in writeups with new std/range values

description: Final validation: confirm all 26 benchmarks pass std >= 0.08 and all submission artifacts are complete
steps: Step 1: Load repo/results/score_matrix_all_tracks.csv and compute std per benchmark - verify ALL 26 have std >= 0.08
Step 2: Verify all 5 writeups exist at repo/WRITEUP_*.md, each under 1500 words, with all required template sections
Step 3: Verify all 5 cover images exist at repo/assets/{track}_cover.png and are valid PNGs
Step 4: Verify all 10 models have scores for all 26 benchmarks (allow max 2 OOM exceptions for Qwen3)
Step 5: Run jupyter nbconvert validation on all 26 benchmark notebooks to confirm no syntax errors
Step 6: Check for .py to .ipynb drift on any recently modified benchmarks
Step 7: git add and commit all changes with message: all benchmarks pass std>=0.08, submission artifacts complete
Step 8: Output final PASS/FAIL checklist per track
